title_vi: Kiến trúc Redis đã phát triển thế nào?

claims.claim_vi: Replication is asynchronous by default; the master does not wait for replicas; WAIT reports how many replicas acknowledged but does not make Redis strongly consistent; replicas are read-only by default.
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment showed OK from the master and WAIT 1 500 returning 0 with the replica stopped, and READONLY when writing to the replica.

claims.claim_vi: Sentinel does monitoring, notification, automatic failover and acts as configuration provider; quorum only detects failure, a failover needs a leader elected by the majority of Sentinels; acknowledged writes can be lost because replication is asynchronous; Sentinel 2 is stable since 2.8.
claims.section: Sentinel capabilities; Configuring Sentinel; Fundamental things to know
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment's Sentinel logs show +sdown, +odown with quorum, +elected-leader, +promoted-slave and +switch-master, and after the master was stopped with SHUTDOWN NOSAVE the replica became master in 3.3 s with down-after-milliseconds 2000.

claims.claim_vi: Redis Cluster splits keys into 16384 hash slots, HASH_SLOT = CRC16(key) mod 16384 except that, when the key holds a non-empty {...} section, only the part between the first { and the following } is hashed (hash tags), clients are redirected with MOVED and ASK, multi-key commands need keys in the same slot, and acknowledged writes can be lost in some windows.
claims.section: Key distribution model; Hash tags; Write safety
claims.verified_by: Read; the experiment showed slot ranges 0-5460/5461-10922/10923-16383, MOVED 6777 for user:2, CROSSSLOT for MSET across slots and the same slot 10778 for {user:1}:cart and {user:1}:orders.

claims.claim_vi: Before 2.0 (tag 1.3.6, March 2010) redis.conf already had RDB save points, appendonly, appendfsync and slaveof; the docs say AOF became available in 1.1.
claims.verified_by: Read the file at the tag; tag commit dated 2010-03-18.

claims.claim_vi: 2.6.0 (Oct 2012) ships sentinel.conf; 2.8.0 released 22 Nov 2013 with new Sentinel code and partial resynchronization of replicas.
claims.verified_by: Read the files at the tags.

claims.claim_vi: 3.0.0 released 1 Apr 2015 with Redis Cluster and the WAIT command; 5.0.0 released 17 Oct 2018 with the stream data type; 6.0.0 GA released 30 Apr 2020 with optional threaded I/O for client socket reads and writes, disabled by default, Redis being mostly single threaded.
claims.section: Release notes headers; redis.conf THREADED I/O
claims.verified_by: Read the files at the tags.

claims.claim_vi: Sentinel provides high availability for non-clustered Redis; Redis Cluster detects a master no longer reachable by the majority of nodes and promotes a replica through its own protocol.
claims.section: Sentinel page description; Cluster specification: Failure detection
claims.verified_by: Read from a partial clone of redis/docs.

design_notes_vi: Bốn bước đánh số, mỗi bước ghi giới hạn nó vá; bốn ghi chú kết quả thử. Tên lệnh không đưa vào chữ của hình (máy kiểm đọc chúng như từ viết tắt), nằm trong bài dưới dạng code. Vẽ bằng scripts/figures.
source_deviations: Source dates persistence and replication to Redis 2.8 in 2013; redis.conf at tag 1.3.6 (March 2010) already has RDB save points, AOF and slaveof, and the docs date AOF to 1.1. The lesson keeps the order as a chain of limits, not as a timeline of first appearances.
Source dates streams to 2017 with Redis 5.0; the 5.0.0 release notes give 17 Oct 2018.
Source does not say that replication is asynchronous or that Sentinel and Cluster can lose acknowledged writes; the lesson adds both with an experiment.
Lesson adds an experiment (replica, three Sentinels, three-node cluster with MOVED, CROSSSLOT and hash tags).
Source presents Sentinel (2013) and Cluster (2015) as consecutive stages; the lesson states that Cluster does its own failover and is an alternative to Sentinel, not a layer on top of it.
